_comment: Mutations that put the pinned-rewrite hole BACK into caddy.config.
The defect (measured 2026-11-07, found by the Copilot engine on panel #3,
condition (f) -- 'an existing test was made permissive'): the pinned-rewrite
rule in tests/test_caddy_public_routes.py ended in a negative lookahead
`(?![A-Za-z0-9])`, which rejected only an ALPHANUMERIC suffix. It therefore
accepted a rewrite target that merely STARTS with a pinned file, and the
companion assertion `assert "rewrite * /source.html" in body` accepted it
too, because the traversal target CONTAINS that substring.
So a caddy.config that rewrote the @source handler at the file holding the
demo credentials would have PASSED the whole test file. The live config
rewrote to exactly /source.html, so this was a regression-TEST gap, not a
live exposure -- but the test is what is supposed to catch the next one.
M1 rewrites @source to /source.html/../demo-build-flag.ts -- a traversal
into the file that holds the demo username/password. Killed by
test_the_source_handler_can_only_serve_source_html and by
test_no_handler_serves_the_mounted_directory_without_a_pinned_path.
M2 rewrites @source to /source.html.bak -- a sibling file that merely
starts with the pinned name. Killed by the same two tests.
The needle is a SINGLE-LINE string and occurs EXACTLY ONCE in caddy.config
(asserted before use); a needle that matched two sites would make the
mutation meaningless.
Run with:  python tools/mutation_harness.py tools/mutations/source_offer_pinned_rewrite.json
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: M1: the @source handler rewrites through the pinned path into the demo-credentials file
M2: the @source handler rewrites to a sibling file that merely starts with the pinned name
